No. 460/2017 Cc No. 48532/16 M/s Nestle India Limited Regd. Office - M/5 -A, Connaught Circle, New Delhi-110001 Manufacturing Unit at- Village Maulinguem (North) Bicholim Taluka-403504, Goa Through its Authorized Representative Sh. Dharmendra Hansraj Kotak Manager, M/s Nestle India Limited ...Revisionist Versus 1. State [Nct of Delhi] 2. Sh. Brijender Pal Saroha, Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi New Delhi ......Respondents Date of Institution : 17.10.2017 Date of reserving Order: 10.07.2023 Date of decision : 19.07.2023 Cr. Rev. No. 460/17 Page 1 of 10 Judgment 1. This is a revision petition against the summoning order dated 04.07.2017 passed by the Ld. Acmm-Ii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.
texts.facts: 3. The summoning order in the present case has been challenged on the ground that the Food Analyst, who prepared the report after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer tested the sample at lab which is not authorized under Section 3(p) and 43(1) of the FSS Act.
texts.arguments: Counsel has relied on paragraph no. 95 of the decision of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Nestle India Limited Vs. The Food Safety and Standards, 2015 SCC OnLine Bom 4713 5. At this juncture, it may be pertinent to refer to Section 3(p) and 43(1) of FSS Act, which reads as follows: 3(p) "food laboratory" means any food laboratory or institute established by the Central or a State Government or any other agency and accredited by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories or an equivalent accreditation agency and recognised by the Food Authority under section 43;... 43(1) The Food Authority may notify food laboratories and research institutions accredited by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories or any other accreditation agency for the purposes of carrying out analysis of samples by the Food Analysts under this Act. 6. Ld. CPP, on the other hand, has argued that this court cannot sit in appeal over the report filed by the Food Analyst. For this it would be relevant to refer to the provisions of Section 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) of the old Act, which read as follows: "23(1A) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:- ............................ (ee) defining the laboratories where samples of articles of food or adulterants may be analysed by public analysts under this act; ....................... (hh) defining the methods of analysis." These provisions were considered by the Apex Court in the case of Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. vs. Food Inspector & Anr, (2011) 1 SCC (Cri) 8. In the said case, the point raised for consideration was whether in the absence of any prescribed and validated method of analysis u/s 23 (1a) (hh) of the Act, could a prosecution be launched against the appellants based on the reports submitted by the Public Analyst using the method of the Director General of Health Services (DGHS). 10. This judgment of the Apex Court was followed by the Kerala High Court in the case of R. Gopalakrishnan Vs. Food Inspector in Criminal Revision Petition No.671/2002 decided on 17.07.2013. Special Leave Petition against the said judgment was preferred in Supreme Court of India, vide Criminal Appeal No. 2476 of 2014, but the same was dismissed. 11. Reliance is also placed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Kerala High Court in Mohanan P. & Others Vs. State of Kerala and Another, Crl. Rev. P.No. 66 of 2011, decided on 25th November, 2021 where the earlier decision in R. Gopalakrishnan (supra) has again been followed. 12. It needs to be emphasized that while on one hand, adulterated food has rampant ramification as it can cause injury and harm to public at large and in order to prevent such adulteration of food, stringent punishments have been prescribed under the Act, but at the same time stringent procedures have also been laid down for determining if the food was adulterated. Paragraph no. 92 of the decision in Nestle India Limited (Supra) has already dealt with the aforesaid question and is quoted hereinbelow for ease of reference: M/S Nestle India Limited vs . State [Nct Of Delhi] on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7762325/ 3 The Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings Private Limited vs. Food Inspector and Another has observed that the provisions are mandatory. The Apex Court in this case held that provisions 23(1-A)(ee) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 for testing the food samples/adulteration are mandatory and not directory. This is more so when Section 43(1) is read with the definition of the words "food laboratory" in Section 3(p) of the FSS Act, 2006. The Apex Court in Pepsico India Holding Private Limited (supra) has observed in para 44 as under:- "44. The High Court also misconstrued the provisions of Sections 23(1-A)(ee) and (hh) in holding that the same were basically enabling provisions and were 1 (2011) 1 SCC 176 not mandatory and could, in any event, be solved by the Central Government by framing the Rules thereunder, by which specified tests to be held in designated laboratories could be spelt out. Consequently, the High Court also erred in holding that the non formulation of rules under the aforesaid provisions of the 1954 Act could not be said to be fatal for the prosecution." 94. Sections 47(1) and 47(5) of the Act read as under:- ... ...95. 16. However, before the Bombay High Court, as recorded in paragraph no. 96 of the judgment, there was no dispute as to whether the laboratories in which food samples were tested were accredited or recognized or not. For a test report to be relevant and before it can be relied upon by a Trial Court, it must be M/S Nestle India Limited vs . State [Nct Of Delhi] on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7762325/ 5 shown that tests were carried out at a notified lab under Section 43(1) of the Act. 18.

The Food Safety and Standards, 2015 SCC OnLine Bom 4713 Ld. CPP, on the other hand, has argued that this court cannot sit in appeal over the report filed by the Food Analyst.
